evals.name: feature-branch-creation
evals.prompt: Create a branch for implementing a new passkey authentication flow in our iOS application, ensuring it follows the team's branching conventions and starts from the latest main branch.
evals.expected_output: A clean branch checkout procedure that fetches the remote state, cuts a branch named feat/passkey-authentication (or ticket-bound equivalent) directly from origin/main, and ensures the working tree is clean without touching main directly.
assertions: Fetches remote state from origin before branching rather than relying on stale local refs.
Uses the feat/ prefix with lowercase kebab-case naming.
Branches directly from origin/main or origin/develop.
Advises against committing directly to protected base branches.

evals.name: emergency-hotfix-isolation
evals.prompt: A critical crash on iOS 26 launch was reported in production version v1.2.0. We need to create a branch to fix this immediately without including unreleased features from main.
evals.expected_output: A targeted hotfix workflow that checks out a hotfix/ branch directly from the production release tag v1.2.0, preserves isolation from main development work, and outlines the dual-merge/cherry-pick path back to main.
assertions: Cuts the branch directly from the production tag v1.2.0 rather than HEAD of main.
Uses the hotfix/ prefix with a descriptive slug.
Strictly limits changes to the minimal crash fix without feature contamination.
Notes that the hotfix must be merged into both the production release path and main.

evals.name: rebase-sync-conflict-hygiene
evals.prompt: My feature branch feat/apple-pay-checkout is 5 commits behind main and ready for review. How should I update it and prepare the pull request?
evals.expected_output: Instructions to fetch origin, rebase the feature branch onto origin/main to maintain linear history, verify that tests pass post-rebase, and push cleanly without merge bubbles.
assertions: Recommends rebasing onto origin/main to keep history linear.
Warns against creating reverse merge commits from main into the feature branch.
Ensures automated tests and builds are verified after the rebase.
Advises using clean Conventional Commits or squash-merging.
